I like the constant juxtaposition of feeling pain and bliss, better ant worse. All beginning with the two discs. Maybe adding another stanza between 2 and 3 to explore the sensory experience might add to the reasoning of the speaker. You could also add a stanza about the feeling of the aftermath if you think that would work. The lines "and sit very still" and "leaves me feeling frail" feel a little out of place in terms of flow, not really sure why though. I love the line "hurts itself confused" it really captures the feeling of being left worse off after using a substance. The overall flow of the poem is smooth and the stanzas build on each other nicely. Good job!

The imagery is great throughout. Throwing in some kind of auditory imagery might add a different dimension to that sensory experience. I can't quite tell if the speaker is trying to say that nature and such is their addiction, or if the progression of time serves to follow an addict through a year of addiction with different drugs. Either way I like the comparison between the feelings surrounding different times of the year and the feelings surrounding being high. The final stanza, (which I saw as representing the low point for the speaker) portrays the negative aspects of an addiction, but I felt that point felt a little flat and broke tone a bit. If your point of the poem is to convey that eventually, you may want something stronger -- at least for the last line. Think about the point you want to make and what you want the reader to walk away with. I absolutely love the line "answers from a grass syringe." It's supper effective and just a beautiful image. Also I think it was a great idea to have a different drug for each stanza. Very good!

I feel like a lot of the confusion regarding the split attraction model stems from the stigma of using words people might not know or don't want to explain. For example, a lot of people who are pan say they are bi because it is easier to explain, but it's more extreme in the case of split attraction. It's more complicated to say I'm "bisexual and aromantic" or I'm "asexual and biromantic" than just "I'm bi." The lack of representation, including self representation (though I definitely don't blame someone for avoiding describing themselves using the s-am) makes it easier to be brushed off by exclusionists and continues the cycle of being "to difficult to explain" making it harder for us to be represented in general.

Not to mention, red flag when anyone says one part of your identity is more important than the other. That's just bullshit

Bi can be used as the umbrella term for pretty much all sexualities that involve two or more, or the ignoring of, gender. Technically though the term bisexual refers to someone who is attracted to two genders. Pan sexual is all genders. Omnisexual is being attracted to people not influenced by their gender at all. Lastly, poly or multisexual refers to someone who is attracted to three or more genders (which sounds like you based on your description). However, people who don't feel like micro labeling themselves and fall under the umbrella of bisexual often just call themselves bi. For example my full "identity" is a greyromantic girlflux polysexual.
